Description

Primary care facilities, public hospital beds and hospital activity for every Moroccan province and prefecture from 2003 to 2024, extracted from all 22 editions of the Ministry of Health yearly report Santé en Chiffres, harmonised to current province codes and checked against every national total printed in the reports.

Morocco’s Ministry of Health has published a yearly statistical report, Santé en Chiffres, since the early 2000s. Its province tables are the only public source on where health facilities and hospital beds are and how they are used, but they are scattered over 22 PDF files whose layout, table numbers and place-name spellings change from one edition to the next. Morocco also created new provinces in 2009 and redrew its regions in 2015.

This dataset puts two decades of those tables into three clean long tables with one code system. Each row names its province, its current region, a comparable unit that stays stable over the whole period, the value, the report page it comes from, and a note when anything was done to it.

Use unit_2004 to build series that span the 2009 province splits: it groups a province with the provinces later carved out of it, so sums by unit_2004 are comparable from 2003 to 2024.

Origin

Produced by Ministère de la Santé et de la Protection Sociale, Kingdom of Morocco

Published in Santé en Chiffres, editions 2003 to 2024 (22 editions, one per data year)

Tables used Primary care facilities (ESSP) by province and setting, and support facilities (public health laboratories, TB centres, reproductive health centres), in every edition. Public hospital beds and activity: one table by province in the 2003-2012 editions, the list of hospitals with province totals in the 2013-2024 editions.

How obtained Tables were read from the PDF reports with scripted parsers that use the position of each number on the page. Province and region names, spelled in many ways across editions, were matched to ISO 3166-2:MA codes with a gazetteer. Every edition was checked against the totals the report itself prints (rows, regions, nation). A printed figure was corrected only when the report’s own sums prove the error; otherwise it is kept as printed and flagged in the note column.

Published on HDR HDR-MA-0002, version 1.0.0

Origin address: https://www.sante.gov.ma (accessed 2026-11-02). Reuse terms: Publicly released reports. No reuse licence is stated in the reports; HDR publishes the extracted figures with attribution and does not re-host the reports.

Variables

facilities.csv

One row per reference date, province, indicator, setting and facility type

Variable Type Description
code string Province or prefecture code (ISO 3166-2:MA; MA-CAS-xxx for the Casablanca prefectures)
province string Province or prefecture name
region_code string Region code, 2015 regional division (12 regions)
region string Region name, 2015 regional division
unit_2004 string Comparable unit over the whole period: the province plus the provinces carved out of it after 2004 (‘+’ joined codes); MA-CAS for all Casablanca prefectures
ref_date string Reference date of the count as printed in the table title (year, or year-month)
year integer Data year of the report edition the value comes from
indicator string primary_care_facilities (ESSP network) or support_facilities
setting string urban, rural or total
category string Facility type (for example urban health centre level 1, CSU-1), or ‘all’ for the total of the setting
value integer Number of facilities
source string Report edition and page
note string What was done to the value, if anything (empty when reproduced as printed)

hospitals.csv

One row per year, province and indicator

Variable Type Description
code string Province or prefecture code (ISO 3166-2:MA)
province string Province or prefecture name
region_code string Region code, 2015 regional division
region string Region name, 2015 regional division
unit_2004 string Comparable unit over the whole period (see facilities.csv)
year integer Year of activity
indicator string beds (functional beds), patient_days, admissions, occupancy_rate (%), average_length_of_stay (days)
value number Value of the indicator; occupancy rate and length of stay are recomputed from the counts
source string Report edition and page(s)
note string How the value was chosen when the report disagrees with itself, flags, and formulas for computed indicators

provinces.csv

One row per province or prefecture code used in the data files

Variable Type Description
code string Province or prefecture code
name string Name
type string province, prefecture or prefecture-arrondissements
region_code string Region code, 2015 regional division
region string Region name, 2015 regional division
unit_2004 string Comparable unit over the whole period
unit_2004_members string All codes grouped in the comparable unit (‘;’ separated)

Known issues

Read these before analysis.

  1. Facility counts are not yearly before 2019. Editions between 2007 and 2017 repeat the table of the previous edition every other year; each count is kept once, under its own reference date (15 dates from 2003 to 2024).
  2. Provinces created in 2009 appear from 2009 or 2011. Before that, their facilities and beds are counted in the parent province. Use unit_2004 for series over the whole period.
  3. Provinces without a hospital have no hospital rows (for example Médiouna and Al Haouz in 2003-2004). Absence means none listed, not missing data: province sums equal the national totals in every year.
  4. Hospital values in 2013-2024 come from hospital lists. When the list and the printed province total disagree, the value that makes the printed region total add up is kept, and the note says so (9 province-years).
  5. A few printed values look implausible but are consistent with the report’s totals, for example Taroudant 2015 (679 beds, against about 300 in 2014 and 2016). They are kept as printed and flagged as ‘isolated spike’ in the note (19 province-years).
  6. Patient days or admissions printed as 0 for a hospital with open beds are set to missing (4 values).
  7. University hospitals (CHU) are included in the hospital figures of their host prefecture (for example Casablanca-Anfa, Rabat, Fès, Marrakech, Oujda, Tanger), which explains jumps when a CHU opens (Oujda 2015, Tanger 2023).

Found an error?

Tell us what you found. A curator compares it with the origin; confirmed errors are listed on this page and fixed in a new version, with credit to you if you wish.
